place: A small town of a few thousand people in the interior of Minas Gerais, Brazil (Cerrado / Atlantic Forest transition)
about: Every place-specific figure the town generator uses for a small town in interior Minas Gerais, Brazil, with its source. State and national statistics stand in for a town where no municipal figure was found; many figures are marked placeholders, with what they were estimated from. Fortnightly wages and payments are the monthly Brazilian figures converted (x 12 / 26) because the structure pays on 14 days. A world for another place and time is another profile; the platform's code holds none of these (docs/profiles.md).

unions.teaching: Together, workers win better pay and conditions than each alone.

sources.currency: Brazilian real, in centavos: written R$ before the amount, or in words as reais (informally contos) and centavos. ISO 4217: BRL, two decimal places. Words "conto" for an informal unit (to confirm usage in Minas Gerais). Brazilians write R$1.234,56 (dot for thousands, comma for decimals); the currency block has no field for that (a structural gap, reported with this profile).
sources.households.age_bands_bps: IBGE, Censo Demografico 2022, SIDRA table 9514 (resident population by sex and age group, Minas Gerais, total 20,539,989), fetched from apisidra.ibge.gov.br on 2026-10-08: shares of the population aged 0 to 99, 85-99 summed from the 85-89, 90-94 and 95-99 groups. State figures stand in for a town of a few thousand (a town is older than the state average; not adjusted).
sources.households.lone_bps: IBGE, Censo 2022, household arrangements (Agencia IBGE de Noticias, "Censo 2022: em 12 anos, proporcao de mulheres responsaveis por domicilios avanca e se equipara a de homens", 2024; reported again in press on the Census release of family arrangements, 2025): one-person households 18.9% (Minas Gerais 18.3%; the national figure is used; to confirm against the SIDRA table).
sources.households.group_bps: IBGE, Censo 2022 (same release): households of several people with no spouse, child or step-child, 6.6% (rounded down to 6.5% so that the five types add to 100%; to confirm).
sources.households.couple_bps: IBGE, Censo 2022 (same release): couples without children 20.2% of households (to confirm).
sources.households.couple_children_bps: IBGE, Censo 2022 (same release): couple with children of both 30.7% plus couple with a child of one spouse 7.2%, 37.9% (to confirm).
sources.households.one_parent_bps: IBGE, Censo 2022 (same release): one parent with children 16.5% (to confirm).
sources.households.children_couple: Placeholder: share of couples with 1, 2 and 3+ children. Not found; estimated as one child most common, from Brazil's fertility of about 1.6 children a woman (IBGE Projecao da Populacao 2024). To replace from Census 2022 tables on children per family (SIDRA).
sources.households.children_one_parent: Placeholder: share of one-parent households with 1, 2 and 3+ children; estimated as for couples, with fewer children in larger sizes. To replace from Census 2022 tables.
sources.households.same_sex_couple_bps: Placeholder: 1.0% of couples; IBGE Census 2022 counted same-sex couples but the share was not retrieved (to confirm; the figure is an order-of-magnitude estimate).
sources.households.lone_parent_female_bps: Placeholder: about 87% of one-parent households headed by a woman (estimate from the Census 2022 release on women as household heads; exact share not retrieved; to confirm).
sources.households.adult_female_bps: Placeholder: about half (as in the reference profile; the 2022 Census has 51.5% women overall, to confirm).
sources.households.child_male_bps: Placeholder: about 51.2% of births male (105 boys per 100 girls, IBGE/SINASC; exact year and figure to confirm).
sources.households.adult_ages: Placeholder: bounds of the adult ages drawn from the census bands (as in the reference profile).
sources.households.mother_age_at_first_birth: Placeholder: the mean age of Brazilian mothers was 27.7 in 2020 (IBGE, Estatisticas do Registro Civil / Projecao da Populacao, reported in the press; to confirm); first births earlier, here 19 to 32.
sources.households.child_max_age: Placeholder: carried over from the reference profile (children stay in the parental home to 24); Brazilian young adults often stay longer (to confirm).
sources.households.group_size: Placeholder: carried over (2 to 3 people in a group household).
sources.life.qx_per_100000: IBGE, Tabuas Completas de Mortalidade do Brasil 2024 (Brasil, homens and mulheres, probability of death q(x,1) per thousand by single year of age 0 to 89; life expectancy at birth 73.3 men, 79.9 women, total 76.6), downloaded as xlsx from ftp.ibge.gov.br/Tabuas_Completas_de_Mortalidade/Tabuas_Completas_de_Mortalidade_2024/xlsx/. Ages 90 to 100: IBGE closes the table at 90+; the tail here is a placeholder extended at the growth of q from age 88 to 89 (capped at 7% a year, and at 0.6). National figures, not Minas Gerais's.
sources.life.illness: Placeholder: carried over unchanged from the reference profile (no Brazilian source searched). To replace from Pesquisa Nacional de Saude 2019 (IBGE) morbidity tables.
sources.life.injury: Placeholder: carried over unchanged from the reference profile (no Brazilian source searched).
sources.life.birth.gestation_days: Biology (about 38 weeks from conception), carried over from the reference profile.
sources.life.birth.female_bps: Placeholder: 100% minus the male share of births (5,120 bps); see households.child_male_bps.
sources.life.treatable: Placeholder: carried over unchanged from the reference profile. To replace from the Ministry of Health, Painel de Mortalidade Evitavel (reducible causes), SIM (to confirm).
sources.life.found_alone_after: Placeholder: carried over unchanged from the reference profile; no Brazilian source searched.
sources.life.work_injury_bps: Placeholder estimate: INSS Anuario Estatistico de Acidentes do Trabalho (AEAT) records on the order of 600,000 registered work accidents a year among about 45 million formal workers, near 1.4% (figures from memory; to confirm); factory above and shop below that mean by assumption.
sources.wages_per_fortnight.shop: The national minimum wage from 1 January 2026, R$1,621 a month (Decreto no 12.797, 31 December 2025, Diario Oficial da Uniao 24 and 31 December 2025), taken as the shop wage (retail floors in collective agreements in Minas Gerais run a little above; to confirm). Converted to 14 days as monthly x 12 / 26 (a gap: Brazil pays by the month).
sources.wages_per_fortnight.factory: Placeholder: R$2,400 a month, estimated at 1.5 times the minimum wage (R$1,621) for an industrial worker in a small interior town. To replace from IBGE, PNAD Continua Anual 2025, rendimento medio do trabalho principal by sector for Minas Gerais (the state mean over all workers was R$3,270 a month in 2025, reported by Itatiaia from IBGE; sector tables not retrieved). Converted to 14 days as x 12 / 26.
sources.wages_per_fortnight.construction: Placeholder: R$2,200 a month (about 1.36 times the minimum wage), estimated; to replace from PNAD Continua sector tables or the CBIC / SINAPI labour cost for Minas Gerais. Converted to 14 days as x 12 / 26.
sources.ordinary_hours_per_week: Constituicao Federal 1988, art. 7, XIII: normal working hours up to eight a day and 44 a week (a proposed constitutional amendment to shorten the week was being debated; check status in 2026; to confirm).
sources.rents_per_month: Placeholder: monthly rent R$550 to R$950 for apartments and R$950 to R$1,300 for houses, estimated for a small interior town in Minas Gerais from typical listings (not sourced; about 30 to 60% of a minimum wage). To replace from IBGE Censo 2022 or POF 2017-18 rent tables for municipalities of under 20,000 people.
sources.spending.saving_bps: Placeholder: about 4% of household disposable income saved, a low figure for Brazil (IBGE, Contas Nacionais Trimestrais, Conta Economica Integrada, household sector; exact current figure not retrieved; to confirm).
sources.spending.wealth_effect_bps_per_year: Placeholder: carried over from the reference profile (a modelling rule).
sources.spending.essentials_per_month: Placeholder: about R$650 a person a month, near the DIEESE Cesta Basica de Alimentos for Belo Horizonte (DIEESE publishes it monthly; the 2026 figure was not retrieved; to confirm).
sources.spending.shops_known: Placeholder: carried over from the reference profile.
sources.spending.shop_search_bps_per_month: Placeholder: carried over from the reference profile.
sources.savings_by_age: Placeholder: the reference profile's distribution scaled by 0.2 (the ratio of Brazilian to Australian household financial wealth and income is much lower; no Brazilian survey of savings by age retrieved). To replace from IBGE POF 2017-18 or Banco Central do Brasil, Relatorio de Cidadania Financeira.
sources.retirement_age: Placeholder / closest fit: 65. Under Emenda Constitucional 103/2019 the permanent old-age retirement age is 65 for men and 62 for women (urban workers, INSS); rural workers 60 and 55 (Lei 8.213/1991, art. 48 par. 1); the low-income old-age benefit (BPC/LOAS, Lei 8.742/1993) starts at 65. The profile holds one age; see the report on structural gaps.
sources.retiree_savings: Placeholder: the reference profile's range scaled by 0.2 (see savings_by_age).
sources.support.pension: The old-age benefit at the minimum wage, R$1,621 a month (Decreto 12.797/2025): paid by INSS as aposentadoria por idade or as the low-income BPC (Lei 8.742/1993), starting at 65; most INSS benefits are one minimum wage. Paid every 30 days (a monthly payment; the reference profile pays every 14). Rural pensioners may start at 60 or 55 and the 13th payment is not modelled.
sources.support.unemployment: Closest fit: the Bolsa Familia, average benefit about R$677.66 per family in June 2026 (Ministerio do Desenvolvimento e Assistencia Social, reported in the press; primary table not opened; to confirm), paid monthly; from age 18. It is a household-income-tested payment to poor families, not an unemployment payment; seguro-desemprego (3 to 5 instalments, formal workers only) cannot be expressed. See the report on structural gaps.
sources.firm_ownership.forms_bps: Placeholder: in a small interior town almost all shops, rented homes and local factories are owned by a person, family or a few partners (SEBRAE, microempresas e empresas de pequeno porte, 99% of firms; to confirm); outside ownership 10 to 30%; no widely held firms.
sources.firm_ownership.closely_held: Placeholder: carried over unchanged from the reference profile.
sources.firm_ownership.widely_held: Placeholder: carried over unchanged from the reference profile.
sources.firm_ownership.direct_holders: Placeholder: carried over unchanged from the reference profile; direct share ownership is far rarer in Brazil (B3, Perfil dos investidores, about 5 million individuals of 160 million adults; to confirm), so this overstates it.
sources.retirement_fund: Placeholder, off unless a town asks for it: the general pension is the state's pay-as-you-go INSS; private pension funds (previdencia complementar) cover a small share of workers. member_bps and share_bps_of_local are estimates (5% and 30%); the drawdown and cost figures are carried over from the reference profile.
sources.industry: Placeholder: carried over from the reference profile (manufacturing labour and input shares, retail purchases and labour shares). To replace from IBGE, Pesquisa Industrial Anual (PIA-Empresa) and Pesquisa Anual de Comercio (PAC), Brazilian national tables, which give wages and intermediate consumption as shares of output.
sources.prices: Placeholder: the reference profile's prices scaled by 0.35, the ratio of hourly shop wages (Brazil R$8.5 against Australia $27.8), so that an item is a comparable amount of work: goods R$35 an item at world prices (the unit the town counts in), inputs R$0.90 a kg, building materials R$0.45 a kg.
sources.labour_force_participation_bps: Placeholder: 72% of 15-64 year olds. IBGE, PNAD Continua, 2nd quarter 2026: participation rate 62.1% (June 2026) of everyone aged 14 and over; rescaled to working age by assumption.
sources.tenancy: Lei do Inquilinato (Lei 8.245/1991): rent may be adjusted once a year (after 12 months) by the contract's index (IGP-M or IPCA); the 30-day notice is a placeholder; a fixed-term lease that runs on without the landlord objecting becomes indeterminate (art. 46 and 56; to confirm the section numbers).
sources.values: Placeholder: carried over unchanged from the reference profile (Schwartz value means set by assumption). To replace from the World Values Survey wave 7 (Brazil, 2018) or the European Social Survey's Schwartz portrait scales (to confirm).
sources.industrial_action: Lei de Greve (Lei 7.783/1989): strikes are allowed after assembly vote and 48 hours' notice (72 hours for essential services); wages for strike days are normally not paid unless negotiated (TST jurisprudence; to confirm). Turnout and pass shares are placeholders carried over.
sources.world_price_process: Placeholder: carried over unchanged from the reference profile (volatility and persistence of world prices).
sources.credit.cash_rate_bps: Banco Central do Brasil, Copom: the Selic target set at 13.75% a year at the 281st meeting, 16 September 2026 (a 25 basis point cut; reported by the press from the Copom statement; the statement not opened; to confirm).
sources.credit.funding_spread_bps: Placeholder: 300 basis points over the Selic, a guess for a retail bank's funding cost and intermediation margin. To replace from Banco Central do Brasil, Relatorio de Economia Bancaria (spread medio).
sources.credit.lending_rate_bps: Placeholder: persons 45% a year (a blend of personal, overdraft and card credit; rotativo much higher, payroll-deductible consignado near 25%), organisations 26% a year. Estimates from memory of the Banco Central do Brasil, Estatisticas Monetarias e de Credito, average interest rates (SGS); the series were not opened; to confirm.
sources.credit.serviceability_buffer_bps: Placeholder: carried over from the reference profile.
sources.credit.max_repayment_share_bps: Persons: 35% of salary, the legal ceiling on deductions for payroll-deductible loans (Lei 10.820/2003 as amended; some 5 points are reserved for a card; to confirm the current limit). Organisations: placeholder carried over.
sources.credit.default_days: Banco Central do Brasil, Resolucao CMN 2.682/1999 (and 4.966/2021): a loan overdue 90 days is treated as impaired (to confirm the current resolution).
sources.credit.max_months: Placeholder: carried over from the reference profile.
sources.credit.reserve: Placeholder: the reference profile's figure scaled by 0.35 (the price ratio). The Banco Central's reserve requirement (compulsorio, 20 to 21% of demand and savings deposits) is a share, not an amount.
sources.opening: Placeholders: the reference profile's opening balances scaled by 0.35 (the ratio of Brazilian to Australian hourly wages). To source if a town's starting capital needs to be real.
sources.town_finance.parks_per_year: Placeholder: the reference profile's figure scaled by 0.35.
sources.town_finance.payment_approval_over: Lei 14.133/2021 (new public procurement law), art. 75, II: direct award without tender for goods and services up to R$62,725.59 as updated for 2025 by Decreto 12.343/2024 (the 2026 update was not retrieved; to confirm), used as the level over which a municipal payment gets more formal approval.
sources.public_finance.income_tax: Receita Federal, personal income tax from 1 January 2026, Lei 15.270/2025 (sanctioned 26 November 2025): income up to R$5,000 a month fully exempt through a reducer, a declining reducer between R$5,000.01 and R$7,350 (978.62 - 0.133145 x income), the ordinary table (7.5% to 27.5%) from R$7,350. The profile is annual and expresses it as three steps: 0% to R$60,000 a year, a 40.81% marginal band to R$88,200 (the 27.5% rate plus the phase-out of the reducer, an approximation that ignores the simplified deduction of R$607.20 a month), then 27.5% (to confirm against the Receita Federal table). Federal law, collected by the federal government, not the municipality.
sources.public_finance.income_tax.levy_bps: Closest fit, placeholder: the employee's social-security contribution to INSS (7.5%, 9%, 12% and 14% bands up to a monthly ceiling about R$8,400 in 2026; 2026 table not retrieved; to confirm), averaged near 9% for typical wages. It funds the INSS pension, not general revenue; no ceiling can be expressed.
sources.public_finance.income_tax.levy_from: Placeholder: the INSS contribution applies from the first real earned.
sources.public_finance.grants_per_resident_per_y: Placeholder: R$3,000 a resident a year. Small municipalities live on transfers: Fundo de Participacao dos Municipios (FPM) and the state's share of ICMS (Tesouro Nacional, Siconfi / Finbra); estimated from memory of per-capita transfers to towns of under 10,000 people; to confirm for a town.
sources.public_finance.rates_per_resident_per_ye: Placeholder: R$120 a resident a year in property tax (IPTU) and fees; IPTU yields very little in small interior towns (Tesouro Nacional, Finbra; per-capita figure to confirm).
sources.public_finance.rates_instalments: Placeholder: IPTU is typically paid in a lump sum or up to ten monthly instalments, set by each municipality's law.
sources.public_finance.rates_penalty_interest_bp: Codigo Tributario Nacional (Lei 5.172/1966), art. 161, par. 1: 1% a month on late tax unless the local law says otherwise (many municipalities add a 2% fine); 12% a year (to confirm).
sources.public_finance.rates_exempt_kinds: Constituicao Federal, art. 150, VI, a: reciprocal immunity of public property from tax; carried over (to confirm that schools and health services are exempt as public bodies).
sources.public_finance.median_house_price: Placeholder: R$250,000 for a modest house in a small interior town in Minas Gerais, estimated; FipeZap and QuintoAndar do not cover such towns. To replace from IBGE Censo 2022 or ITBI transaction values.
sources.services.waste_per_person_per_day_g: ABRELPE, Panorama dos Residuos Solidos no Brasil (2022-2024 editions): about 1.04 kg of household waste per person per day (figure from memory; to confirm).
sources.services.landfill_levy_per_tonne: Closest fit, placeholder: Brazil has no landfill levy; municipalities pay a disposal (tipping) fee to a sanitary landfill, about R$120 a tonne for small towns (estimate; to confirm).
sources.services.council_staff_per_1000: Placeholder: 10 council staff per 1,000 residents on works and services. Small Brazilian municipalities employ far more in total, including teachers and health workers (IBGE, MUNIC; to confirm).
sources.services.collect_seconds_per_10kg: Placeholder: carried over from the reference profile.
sources.services.asset_life_years: Placeholder: carried over from the reference profile.
sources.services.upkeep_hours_per_week_per_asset: Placeholder: carried over from the reference profile.
sources.services.complain_bps: Placeholder: carried over from the reference profile.
sources.unions.membership_bps: Placeholder: unionisation of employed people in Brazil is about 8 to 9% (IBGE, PNAD Continua, Caracteristicas adicionais do mercado de trabalho, 2022 and 2023: 9.2% in 2022; later figure to confirm); sector splits estimated (public administration highest).
sources.unions.dues_per_month: Placeholder: about R$30 a month (a typical monthly member contribution of about 1% of a low wage). The compulsory union tax was made voluntary by Lei 13.467/2017.
sources.unions.resignation_notice_days: Placeholder: 0; a member may leave at any time (Lei 13.467/2017 made union dues voluntary; to confirm).
sources.unions.claim_margin_bps: Placeholder: carried over from the reference profile.
sources.unions.meeting_every_days: Placeholder: carried over from the reference profile.
sources.groups.kinds: Placeholder: carried over from the reference profile (kinds, names and rhythms of groups). Religion's held_at_start_bps: 83.6% of people aged 10 and over are Catholic (56.7%) or evangelical (26.9%) (IBGE, Censo Demografico 2022, Religiao, released June 2025). The names of Brazilian groups (for example a football club) are not changed.
sources.groups.taking_part_bps: Placeholder: carried over from the reference profile.
sources.groups.leave_notice_days: Placeholder: carried over from the reference profile.
sources.groups.per_kind_per_1000_people: Placeholder: carried over from the reference profile.
sources.elections: Constituicao Federal art. 29, II and Lei 9.504/1997: a mayor (prefeito) is elected directly for four years, in one round by plurality in municipalities of under 200,000 voters; voting is compulsory from 18 to 70. Municipal elections were held on 6 October 2024; the next is October 2028. Turnout 78.3% is the national first-round figure in 2024 (TSE; abstention about 21.7%; from memory; to confirm); stand_bps and news_readers_bps are placeholders carried over.
sources.health: Doctors: placeholder, 1.2 per 1,000 for a small interior town (Brazil has about 2.9 doctors per 1,000 overall, concentrated in capitals: CFM/FMUSP, Demografia Medica no Brasil 2025; to confirm). Wage: placeholder, a salaried SUS municipal doctor R$12,000 a month, converted to 14 days (x 12 / 26). The clinic stands for the Unidade Basica de Saude and the nearest hospital (a liberty). Consultation length, care-seeking and treatment shares are placeholders carried over from the reference profile.
sources.round: Placeholder hours: 8 to 17 (an hour for lunch), Monday to Friday, for everyone (many shops open Saturdays; a liberty); school 7 to 12, the usual morning shift (LDB, Lei 9.394/1996: at least four hours a day, 800 hours over 200 days). Travel speeds and road figures are carried over from the reference profile (physics: a 25 m cell on foot in 18 seconds; roads slower than the reference's by assumption), and the roads budget is scaled by 0.35 (placeholder).
sources.ownership.house_owner_bps: IBGE, Censo 2022: 71.3% of the 72.5 million private permanent occupied dwellings were owned (72.7% of people lived in owned homes; 20.9% in rented homes). National figure, not for houses only; to confirm for Minas Gerais.
sources.ownership.mortgage_bps_by_age: Placeholder: Brazilian home-ownership is mostly outright (houses built over time, inherited), few owners have a mortgage (the Caixa Economica Federal and the SBPE finance a small share); shares by age are estimates.
sources.ownership.mortgage_payment_per_month: Placeholder: R$1,100 a month, estimated for a modest financed house.
sources.ownership.mortgage_rate_bps: Placeholder: about 11.5% a year plus the TR, near Caixa's SBPE rate (Caixa Economica Federal, financiamento imobiliario; current rate not retrieved; to confirm).
sources.ownership.market: Deposit 20% (SBPE financing up to 80% of a house's value; Caixa; to confirm), costs 5% (ITBI of 2 to 3% plus registry and notary fees; to confirm), 360-month term (up to 35 years). Other market parameters (buy rate, relisting, price cuts) are placeholders carried over.
sources.utilities.water.litres_per_person_per_da: SNIS, Diagnostico dos Servicos de Agua e Esgotos: about 150 litres per inhabitant per day nationally (2022 figure of about 148; from memory; to confirm).
sources.utilities.water.price_per_kl: Placeholder: R$5.00 a kilolitre of water. Copasa (and Arsae-MG, its regulator) applied a 6.56% adjustment from 22 January 2026; the residential tariff table was not retrieved, so the level is an estimate; to replace from Arsae-MG resolution tables.
sources.utilities.water.service_per_quarter: Closest fit, placeholder: Copasa bills a minimum monthly charge covering a first block of consumption rather than a service charge; R$60 a quarter here (to replace from the tariff table).
sources.utilities.water.river_inflow_kl_per_cell: Placeholder: carried over from the reference profile.
sources.utilities.water.river_decay_bps_per_day: Placeholder: carried over from the reference profile.
sources.utilities.water.river_flow_bps_per_day: Placeholder: carried over from the reference profile.
sources.utilities.energy.kwh_per_household_per_d: Placeholder: about 5 kWh a household a day (about 150 kWh a month; EPE, Anuario Estatistico de Energia Eletrica, residential average near 160 kWh a month; from memory; to confirm). Rounded to an integer.
sources.utilities.energy.price_per_kwh: Placeholder: about R$1.00 a kWh including taxes. ANEEL homologated the Cemig Distribuicao annual tariff review on 26 May 2026 (low-voltage average effect +5.21%, overall +6.50%), in force from 28 May 2026; the residential tariff in R$/kWh was not retrieved; to confirm.
sources.utilities.energy.supply_per_day: Closest fit, placeholder: Brazil bills a minimum "custo de disponibilidade" of 30, 50 or 100 kWh a month (single, two or three phase; ANEEL REN 1000/2021) rather than a daily supply charge; R$0.50 a day here.
sources.utilities.energy.grid_price_per_kwh: Placeholder: R$0.60 a kWh, the credit a small solar generator receives under the compensation system (Lei 14.300/2022; credits against the energy component of the tariff; to confirm).
sources.utilities.energy.grid_emissions_g_per_kw: Placeholder: about 40 g of CO2 a kWh, the Brazilian grid being mostly hydro (Ministerio da Ciencia, Tecnologia e Inovacao, Fator medio mensal de emissao do SIN; the 2023 annual average was near 39 g; from memory; to confirm).
sources.climate: Weather drawn for each run (docs/behaviour/weather.md). rain_by_month_bps: the interior of Minas Gerais has a wet season from October to March and a dry season from April to September (INMET, Normais Climatologicas 1991-2020; shape estimated, peak flow in January and lowest in August; to confirm against ANA river-flow series). Storms, droughts and heatwaves are placeholders carried over: the structure has no wet-season weighting (a gap); Minas Gerais has had severe flooding (January 2020, January 2022, S2iD / Defesa Civil records) and a water crisis (the Southeast drought of 2014 to 2016; to confirm). Heat-wave months set to September to March (INMET heat-wave warnings in the dry spring; placeholder).
sources.hazards: Placeholder: carried over from the reference profile (river bank capacity, spill and flood thresholds, wetland soak). Flood records for Minas Gerais municipalities: Defesa Civil / S2iD; to source.
sources.crime.detection_bps: Placeholder: about 10% of thefts solved. The clearance rate for property crime in Brazil is low (Forum Brasileiro de Seguranca Publica, Anuario Brasileiro de Seguranca Publica 2026, released July 2026; no clearance figure retrieved). To replace from the Anuario or Minas Gerais SEJUSP data.
sources.crime.police_per_1000: Placeholder: about 1.9 police a thousand people (the Policia Militar of Minas Gerais has about 40,000 officers for 20.5 million people; from memory; Anuario Brasileiro de Seguranca Publica, efetivo; to confirm). The state police (military for patrol, civil for investigation) stand in for one station.
sources.crime.officer_wage_per_fortnight: Placeholder: R$5,500 a month for a military police soldier or corporal in Minas Gerais (estimate; to confirm against the state's Lei de remuneracao), converted to 14 days (x 12 / 26).
sources.justice.hearing_after_days: Placeholder: about 45 days. The Juizado Especial Civel (Lei 9.099/1995) is the small-claims court for tenancy and consumer disputes up to 40 minimum wages; the Justica do Trabalho handles wage claims; Conselho Nacional de Justica, Justica em Numeros gives times (to source).
sources.justice.apply_bps: Placeholder: carried over; Brazil has a high labour-claims rate (CNJ, Justica em Numeros; to source).
sources.education.school_ages: Constituicao Federal art. 208, I (Emenda Constitucional 59/2009): basic education is compulsory and free from 4 to 17.
sources.education.students_per_teacher: Placeholder: 17 students a teacher (INEP, Censo Escolar 2024, alunos por docente in municipal schools; from memory; to confirm).
sources.education.school_days_per_year: Lei de Diretrizes e Bases (Lei 9.394/1996), art. 24, I: at least 200 school days a year and 800 hours.
sources.education.hours_per_day: LDB art. 34: at least four hours of actual teaching a day in primary school.
sources.education.teacher_wage_per_fortnight: The national salary floor (piso) of public basic-education teachers, R$5,130.63 a month for 40 hours a week in 2026 (Ministerio da Educacao, portaria of January 2026, a 5.4% rise from R$4,867.77; reported by the press), converted to 14 days (x 12 / 26).
sources.education.attainment: IBGE, PNAD Continua Educacao 2025 (2nd quarter 2025), people aged 25 and over: no schooling 6.0%, primary not finished 31.4%, primary finished 8.1%, secondary not finished 4.8%, secondary finished 28.2%, higher education not finished 4.2%, higher finished 17.4% (sum 100.1%; the first two are merged and shown as 37.3%). Years of schooling: 5 for the first group, 9 for primary, 12 for secondary and 16 for degree are the legal lengths (placeholder for 5, 10 and 13). National figure.
sources.education.return_per_year_bps: Placeholder: about 10% a year, carried over from the reference profile; Brazilian estimates of the return to schooling are higher, 10 to 15% (for example Menezes-Filho, various; to confirm).

sources.nature.species: Callithrix penicillata (native to the Cerrado and Atlantic Forest edge). In Cerrado habitats (cerradao and dense cerrado) of the Brazilian Central Plateau: groups of 4 to 11, home range 8.25 to 18.5 ha, density 0.4 to 0.82 individuals a hectare, higher in gallery forest (Miranda and Faria 2001, Brazilian Journal of Biology / Brazilian Journal of Biology 61; found via search, paper not opened; to confirm). Density 0.8 in woodland and riverbank and 0.4 in scrub; growth, mortality and dispersal are placeholders. | Myrmecophaga tridactyla, Vulnerable (IUCN Red List; ICMBio Livro Vermelho 2018; to confirm). Density about 0.2 to 0.4 animals per square kilometre in Cerrado (0.002 to 0.004 per hectare) and a home range of the order of 300 ha (Medri and Mourao 2005 and Cerrado studies; from memory; to confirm). Growth, mortality and dispersal are placeholders (one pup a year; road-kill is a leading cause of death). | Turdus rufiventris (sabia-laranjeira), the national bird of Brazil, common and conspicuous in towns and woodland. Density and home range are placeholders (no source retrieved; a typical passerine territory is about 1 ha). | Caiman latirostris, found in wetlands and rivers of the Atlantic Forest and Cerrado; in Rio Doce State Park, Minas Gerais, an encounter rate of 4.01 individuals a kilometre of water body was recorded (found via search from Brazilian herpetological literature, paper not opened; to confirm). Converted by the cell size to about 1.6 an hectare of riverbank cell (an estimate); the wetland density, home range, growth and mortality are placeholders. IUCN Least Concern (to confirm). Tolerance of pollution is a placeholder.
sources.fertility_per_10000: Placeholder: births a year per 10,000 women by 5-year age group, an estimate shaped to Brazil's total fertility rate of 1.57 children a woman in 2023 (IBGE, Projecao da Populacao 2024 / Estatisticas do Registro Civil, as reported in the press; the age-specific rates themselves were not retrieved; to replace from IBGE Projecao da Populacao 2024, taxas especificas de fecundidade). The five-year rates sum to a total fertility of about 1.56.
